corpusIdConvention._whatThisIsNot: NOT MEASUREMENT AND NOT PROVENANCE. The 'corpus' block above records one corpus that exists and was measured, and .github/scripts/check-testbed-references.ps1 pins its four values across three files. THIS block is a naming rule plus the ids reserved under it, each with a status saying whether that corpus exists and citing where that is recorded; most of the ids - the fixture populations below - describe corpora that DO NOT EXIST YET. It is separated rather than folded into 'corpus' precisely so the two can never be confused: nothing here is a figure this file vouches for - a status cites the runbook, and a seed, anchor or itemCount is filled in only from a manifest's header line - and adding a row here is not a measurement.
corpusIdConvention._why: A manifest is named after the CORPUS, not after the guest, and Testbed/host/Copy-FromGuest.ps1 lands every guest's pull in one shared directory. One guest, harmless. Two guests sharing a corpus id, and the second pull silently replaces the first's manifest - which is the EntryID allowlist corpus-teardown requires and the file corpus-verify reads for freshness, so losing it removes the only safe way to remove that corpus from a real store. The fix is not a per-guest subdirectory: the two corpora genuinely ARE different populations, on different machines with different index state, and they already have to be told apart in each machine's settings file and in every measurement. Giving them one id and disambiguating by directory would paper over that.
corpusIdConvention.manifestFileNameNote: This is what makes Copy-FromGuest.ps1's default 'corpus-*.jsonl' include pattern work, and it is the whole of the collision fix: distinct ids give distinct file names, so the shared destination stops being a shared file. Copy-FromGuest.ps1 also REFUSES to replace a manifest whose content differs unless -Force is passed, as a backstop for the day somebody reuses an id anyway.
corpusIdConvention.idCharacterRule: ASCII letters, digits, '-' or '_' - enforced by CorpusPlan's constructor, because the id lands inside the subject tag that teardown matches ordinally. Prefer '-': '_' is DASL's single-character wildcard, which turns CorpusPlan.DaslSubjectFragment from an exact match into a superset.
corpusIdConvention.namingRule: Name the corpus after the PROPERTY THAT DIFFERS, not after a sequence number. 'vm2' is opaque and only works because there is one of it; with two guests the id has to carry which population it is, since it is what appears in a measurement's comparison scope, in every corpus subject, and in the manifest file name a human reads in a shared directory.

populations._what: The ids reserved for the curated FIXTURE populations the generator builds into each guest's hub, bystander and identity stores (corpus-build --population hub|bystander|identity; Q70, 2026-09-24; Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 3b). Same id rules and same reason as above: a population's manifest is corpus-<id>.jsonl, it lands in the same shared pull directory, and it is the only allowlist corpus-teardown will delete from - and the hub is not a store anybody can simply delete and recreate, because it is the dummy account's delivery store. Nothing here is a measurement. The three OutlookAI-Unindexed populations were built ONCE, 2026-09-24, by generator v1, and NOT cleanly (Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 4.1, step 6): that state survives only in checkpoint CP-11-POPULATIONS-BUILT-WITH-FAULTS, as evidence, and the guest is rolled back before any v2 build - so every status below is what a live run can rely on. Since 2026-10-03 that is OutlookAI-Unindexed's three, built by v2 without the undated items (Q98 (a); Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 4.1d, CP-12B-POPULATIONS-V2), and OutlookAI-Indexed's three, built the same morning with the hub's and the bystander's undated CONTACTS (Q98 (f); section 4.2c, CP-16C-POPULATIONS-V2).
populations._seedAndAnchor: A population's seed is fixed per id below, so a rebuild reproduces it byte-for-byte. Its anchor is NOT fixed: the hub population is rebuilt against the moment a run starts, because its newest item is what makes the index frontier one minute old, and a frontier younger than the guest's UTC offset is the only kind LiveIndexSearchTests.Staleness_SelfReportsPlausibleFrontier can catch a local-time misreading with. The anchor goes in the manifest header, which is where a rebuild reads it from. The rebuild is a script step, decided 2026-09-24: Testbed/guest/Reset-HubPopulation.ps1, first in every run, and the frontier test fails on a hub it did not rebuild.
populations._version: Generator v2 (2026-09-24): besides its dated mail, the hub carries 12 UNDATED items - 4 appointments, 4 contacts and 4 tasks, none with a delivery time - and the bystander 42 (14 of each), so the three LiveOrderKeyCollationTests measure undated rows instead of running weak. No unsent drafts, although the maintainer's decision (question A, option (a)) named them: measured on OutlookAI-Unindexed the same day, a new unsent mail item's first save is filed in the profile's DEFAULT store's Drafts, and a population is never built into the default store, so a draft cannot be made in one without writing into another store first. Dated items are byte-identical to v1's. A v1 manifest's shape key does not match a v2 generator. SWITCHED OFF 2026-10-03 (Q98 (a)): in a PST those kinds turned out DATED, and Outlook will not remove the date (Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 3b), so the populations are built without them - the hub 56 items, the bystander 300, the identity store 8 - behind one plan parameter, CorpusPlanOptions.IncludeUndatedItems, off by default. A population without them is a prefix of one with them, under the same shape key. They come back only if the indexed guest shows the index leaves those kinds undated (Q98 (f)). IT DID, FOR CONTACTS ALONE (measured 2026-10-03: an appointment and a task are indexed with System.Message.DateReceived = their creation time, a contact with none), so on the INDEXED guest the hub and the bystander carry undated contacts - the same twelve and forty-two undated rows, every one a contact, after the dated items: 68 and 342 items - behind a second plan parameter, CorpusPlanOptions.IncludeUndatedContacts (--undated-contacts), which IS part of the shape key ('|u:contacts' at its end). Decided on the maintainer's behalf the same day (D62 of Docs/overnight-review-2026-10-03.md); the unindexed guest keeps its populations without them.

corpusIdConvention.open: Whether vm-indexed and vm-unindexed should share a seed and anchor is STILL NOT SETTLED - it is item 16 of Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 8, and nothing here decides it. Sharing them makes the two stores directly comparable, which is probably what is wanted; that is a reason, not a decision. The ids are distinct either way, which is the point: two corpora may share every generator parameter and still must not share an id, because the id is what names the POPULATION - one machine's store - and those are two different stores whichever way the seed question goes.

expectedPlan._note: What 'corpus-plan' prints for the four parameters in the 'corpus' block - NOT for anything in 'corpusIdConvention', whose corpora have no plan recorded here (the two guests' corpora exist; Corpus B's seed, anchor and itemCount were read off its manifest on 2026-10-03 and are recorded there, and so are Corpus A's - the 160,000-item corpus built on OutlookAI-Indexed the same day, whose record carries its own expectedPlan and buildCost). Committed so a rebuilder can tell a correct rebuild from a subtly different one without having the old store to compare against. check-testbed-references.ps1 does not recompute these - running the tool needs a toolchain - but Testbed/guest/Build-Corpus.ps1 prints them beside the live plan.

liveTestSettings._what: The per-guest values for Testbed/live-test-settings.template.json, one section per guest, keyed by VM name. 'pwsh -File Testbed/host/New-LiveTestSettings.ps1 -VMName <name>' renders that guest's gitignored live-test-settings.json from them. Unlike the file it renders, this section IS committed - which is safe only because a test guest's stores are synthetic: created by this directory's own scripts and named after nothing real. NEVER put a store name from a working Outlook profile here. The maintainer's own settings file stays hand-written and gitignored, and the renderer refuses to write anywhere it could live.
liveTestSettings._fill: Every value that begins '<FILL' is a placeholder, and the renderer REFUSES a guest while any remains, naming each one. They are store names and corpus build parameters that can only be READ OFF THE GUEST - over COM, from the TIER profile the live tier runs under. OutlookAI-Unindexed's were read on 2026-09-24 (its _readOffTheGuest says when and how, and it holds no placeholder now); OutlookAI-Indexed's have not been read yet, so every placeholder left is in its section. Corrected 2026-09-27; this said 'and nobody has read them yet'. Do not type the name you expect to be there; copy the one Outlook reports. Declare only stores that profile mounts: a declared store the running profile does not have is censused, is not found, and refuses the tier. The renderer cannot check that from the host and says so every time it runs.
liveTestSettings._blocks: subjectOnlyProbe, corpus and mailSink take either an object carrying every field, or null for 'this guest has none'. Never a partial object: the loader refuses one and so does the renderer. null leaves the block out of the rendered file, which the loader reads as absent. When this guest's corpus is not built, or its tier profile does not mount the corpus store, set corpus to null. When it IS declared, the renderer holds corpusId, seed, anchorUtc and itemCount against corpusIdConvention above - so a corpus whose seed, anchor and itemCount that record does not hold yet (null there means not recorded) has to be recorded there first, from its manifest's header line.
liveTestSettings._decided: Some values are filled in because they are recorded DECISIONS, not facts to read off a machine. machineProfile is Portable: a guest declares no Production population, and Portable is the profile whose missing populations announce PROVED NOTHING instead of refusing. expectedDelegateStoreDisplayNames is empty: DelegateStore is the one capability no test machine can be given (Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 5). mailSink is the loopback block - submit 127.0.0.1:25, retrieve 127.0.0.1:110, a 2,000 ms connect timeout, where Testbed/guest/Install-MailSink.ps1 binds Inbucket - once a guest's sink has reported SINK-READY, and null until then: the guests DO get a sink, decided 2026-09-24 (Q71, section 1.4), reversing the no-sink decision of 2026-09-15; and a sink block pointing at a listener that is not there refuses the whole tier at start. Both guests reported SINK-READY on 2026-09-24 (sections 4.1 step 3 and 4.2 step 3), OutlookAI-Indexed again on its rebuilt line on 2026-09-27 (section 4.2b step 4.3). corpus.corpusId is the id corpusIdConvention assigns to this guest, and corpus.windowDays copies Testbed/live-test-settings.example.json - EXCEPT on OutlookAI-Indexed, which declares [30, 60]: decided on the maintainer's behalf 2026-10-03 (D103 of Docs/overnight-review-2026-10-03.md), because no live test asks that guest's corpus a 7-day question and declaring one made the tier refuse a week after every rebuild (the corpus block's _note). hubPopulationManifestPath is C:\OutlookAI-Q5\corpus-<id>.jsonl for the hub id corpusIdConvention.populations assigns this guest, by the same naming rule as every manifest: the hub is rebuilt from it before every run (Testbed/guest/Reset-HubPopulation.ps1, decided 2026-09-24), and the frontier test fails on a hub nobody rebuilt. On the INDEXED guest, probeTerm and three of subjectOnlyProbe's four fields are the population generator's own constants (CorpusPopulation.ProbeTerm, SubjectOnlyTerm, SubjectOnlySenderFragment and the hub's Notices folder) - T1/LiveTestSettingsTemplateTests holds them equal - and only the store, which is the hub, is read off the guest. On the UNINDEXED guest nothing is indexed, so indexedStoreDisplayNames is [], probeTerm is empty and subjectOnlyProbe is null: the index tests are deselected there, and the loader turns any that run anyway into a refusal. throwawayStoreDisplayName is throwaway@vm.invalid on both guests (Q96 (iv), 2026-10-03): the data file with no Drafts folder that Testbed/guest/Reset-ThrowawayStore.ps1 recreates in the tier profile before every run, under exactly that name, so the created-folder proof (T2/LiveCreatedFolderTests) has a store whose Drafts folder the product must create and report. It is a decision, not a fact read off a guest - the script makes the store - and it is in no other list on purpose (the loader refuses it in any). Change any of them only with the decision behind it.
liveTestSettings._indexedOrder: indexedStoreDisplayNames on the indexed guest is [hub, bystander, corpus] in THAT order, and the renderer holds it: several index tests read entry 0, which must be the hub whose population carries senders and attachments; the exclude-subfolders measurement reads the first non-hub entry, which must be the bystander whose population has subfolders. Every entry but the corpus must be named as an .invalid address - the product finds a small store in the index only through mail addressed to it, and only for a name shaped like an address. The identity account's store is WATCHED and not in this list: it is written to by the identity tests and holds only its tiny population.
